content.value_statement: Production issues are hard to triage when errors, logs, and alerts are disconnected. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through monitoring setup, grouping, alerting, recovery, and dashboards.
actual_capabilities: Assesses current error handling, logging frameworks, monitoring setup, and error patterns.
Provides Sentry and custom error tracking integration patterns.
Designs structured logging with file, console, and Elasticsearch transport examples.
Defines alert rules, cooldowns, and channel routing for production incidents.
Explains error grouping, performance impact tracking, recovery flows, and dashboard components.
limitations: Requires access to runtime behavior, logs, or monitoring configuration for best results.
Does not replace a production incident response process or on-call ownership.
Example integrations still need service-specific credentials and privacy review.
Generated recommendations must be tested in staging before production rollout.

use_cases.title: Set Up Service Error Tracking
use_cases.description: Add error capture, context enrichment, and safe redaction to a backend service.

use_cases.title: Improve Incident Alerting
use_cases.description: Create actionable alert thresholds, cooldowns, and routing for production failures.

use_cases.title: Standardize Observability Practices
use_cases.description: Define repeatable logging, grouping, dashboard, and recovery patterns across teams.

prompt_templates.title: Review Current Monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my service's current error monitoring and identify missing capture, logging, alerting, and dashboard coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Add Structured Logging
prompt_templates.prompt: Design structured logging for this service, including log levels, request context, redaction rules, and storage targets.

prompt_templates.title: Design Alert Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Create production alert rules for error rate, latency, memory, and disk risks with thresholds, cooldowns, and escalation channels.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Observability Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a phased observability rollout that covers tracking integration, grouping, performance impact, recovery strategy, dashboard design, and validation.

output_examples.input: A Node service has console logs, no alerting, and repeated production exceptions.
output: Assessment: error capture is incomplete, logging is not structured, and no ownership path exists.
Plan: add centralized tracking, redact sensitive fields, group repeated errors, and route critical alerts.

output_examples.input: An API team receives too many low-value alerts after deployments.
output: Alert review: thresholds are too broad and cooldowns are missing.
Recommendation: separate warning and critical rules, add deployment context, and route only actionable failures.

output_examples.input: A platform team wants a shared error dashboard.
output: Dashboard outline: error rate, total errors, affected users, resolution time, top errors, and active alerts.
Next step: connect dashboard metrics to grouped errors and incident ownership.

best_practices: Redact secrets, tokens, cookies, and personal data before sending telemetry.
Use severity levels, cooldowns, and ownership rules so alerts stay actionable.
Validate error capture and alert routing in staging before production rollout.
anti_patterns: Logging raw request bodies, cookies, tokens, or personal data into error events.
Routing every warning to urgent channels without thresholds or cooldowns.
Adding dashboards without owners, triage steps, or recovery actions.

faq.question: Does this skill fix application bugs directly?
faq.answer: No. It helps capture, group, alert, and diagnose errors so teams can fix issues faster.

faq.question: Can it work with Sentry?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes Sentry integration patterns and custom tracking service examples.

faq.question: Does it require production access?
faq.answer: It needs relevant runtime, log, or monitoring context to produce accurate recommendations.

faq.question: How does it handle sensitive data?
faq.answer: It recommends redaction and warns against logging secrets, tokens, or personal data.

faq.question: Can it design alert routing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers thresholds, severity, cooldowns, and channels such as Slack, email, or paging systems.

faq.question: Is it useful for dashboards?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines metrics, live error streams, trends, distributions, top errors, and active alert views.
